summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2 and node3 (standbys) on Alpine Linux, with all replication traffic carried over TLS using a cluster-specific CA and mandatory client-certificate authentication. Verified TLS enforcement, live replication, and full recovery after a one-at-a-time restart of every node.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql16 + postgresql16-openrc + openssl on node1, node2, node3
Created a self-signed cluster CA (ca.key/ca.crt) on node1
Issued per-node server certificates (CN/SAN matching node1/node2/node3 hostnames and IPs) signed by the CA
Issued a client certificate (CN=replicator) signed by the CA for the replication role

Distributed ca.crt, the replicator client cert/key, and per-node server certs to node2/node3 via base64 exec transfer (root SSH login was locked, so file transfer used direct exec calls) with sha256 checksum verification

Initialized the primary data directory on node1, configured postgresql.conf (ssl=on, ssl_cert_file/ssl_key_file/ssl_ca_file, wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, max_replication_slots) and pg_hba.conf (hostssl replication replicator <ip>/32 cert clientcert=verify-full)
Created the replicator role with REPLICATION LOGIN
Started PostgreSQL on node1 and confirmed SSL is active
Ran pg_basebackup from node2 and node3 against node1 over TLS (sslmode=verify-ca, client cert/key, CA rootcert), which also wrote primary_conninfo with TLS settings and standby.signal
Created physical replication slots (node2_slot, node3_slot) and re-based node2 after an initial WAL-segment gap, then bound node3 to its slot via primary_slot_name
Configured matching ssl settings and pg_hba.conf on node2 and node3, started PostgreSQL on both as standbys
Verified pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both standbys streaming with ssl=t in pg_stat_ssl, and that data written on the primary (repltest.t) replicates to both standbys

Proved certificate enforcement: a connection with no client cert failed with 'connection requires a valid client certificate', and a connection with a rogue self-signed CN=replicator cert failed with 'SSL error: tlsv1 alert unknown ca'

Executed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id, service status, replication state, and data baselines on all three nodes; restarted node2, then node3, then node1 one at a time via native `reboot` (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect); polled each node until exec access returned; confirmed changed boot_id on each node; verified PostgreSQL restarted at boot, standby recovery mode, replication streaming resumed with active slots, and data integrity after each restart
Performed a final post-restart write on the primary and confirmed it replicated to both standbys

evidence.requirement: Streaming replication established with node1 as writable primary, node2/node3 as standbys
evidence.summary: node1 initialized as primary with wal_level=replica and started; node2/node3 base-backed up from node1 and started with standby.signal; pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both node2 and node3 in 'streaming' state; pg_is_in_recovery()=t on both standbys.

evidence.requirement: Cluster-specific CA created and used to sign all TLS certs
evidence.summary: Self-signed CA (CN=PostgreSQL-Replication-CA) generated on node1; server certs for node1/node2/node3 and the replicator client cert issued and signed by this CA (visible via openssl x509 -subject/-ext output).

evidence.requirement: Replication traffic actually encrypted with TLS
evidence.summary: postgresql.conf has ssl=on on all nodes; pg_basebackup succeeded only via sslmode=verify-ca with client cert; pg_stat_ssl joined to pg_stat_activity shows ssl=t for both replication connections on the primary.

evidence.requirement: Only peers presenting a CA-issued certificate are accepted for replication
evidence.summary: pg_hba.conf enforces 'hostssl replication replicator <ip>/32 cert clientcert=verify-full'; a connection attempt with no client cert failed with 'connection requires a valid client certificate', and one with a rogue self-signed CN=replicator cert failed with 'SSL error: tlsv1 alert unknown ca' -- proving only CA-signed certs are accepted.

evidence.requirement: Data actually replicates end-to-end from primary to both standbys
evidence.summary: A row inserted on node1 (repltest.t) appeared on both node2 and node3 via SELECT.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 98b5e157...; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; post-restart boot_id f6b911ae... (changed); PostgreSQL restarted at boot, primary not in recovery, SSL on, repltest data intact, both standbys reconnected streaming with active slots.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 75facb81...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id d6051aaa... (changed); PostgreSQL restarted at boot, pg_is_in_recovery=t, repltest data intact, and primary's pg_stat_replication/pg_replication_slots show node2 streaming again with an active slot.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 86c4b668...; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id f4e2e2b4... (changed); PostgreSQL restarted at boot, pg_is_in_recovery=t, repltest data intact, and primary's pg_stat_replication/pg_replication_slots show node3 streaming again with an active slot.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart write replication still functioning across the full cluster
evidence.summary: After all three restarts, a new row inserted on node1 replicated to both node2 and node3, confirming end-to-end TLS-encrypted, certificate-gated streaming replication survived the restart cycle.
